name: A Tokyo suburb
blurb: A suburban garden in Setagaya, western Tokyo: a clipped camellia hedge, a persimmon and a camphor tree over a small lawn and a stone-edged pond, visited by bulbuls, white-eyes, tits, starlings and crows by day, by raccoon dogs and red foxes after dark, and by common toads in the warm months.

facts.text: Setagaya is one of the 23 special wards of Tokyo, in the west of the metropolis on the Musashino plateau above the Tama River.

source.title: Wikipedia: Setagaya
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Setagaya", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Tokyo, including Setagaya, has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa), with hot humid summers and cool winters with occasional cold spells.

source.title: Wikipedia: Tokyo
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Tokyo", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The public centroid of Setagaya at 35.65 N, 139.65 E lies about 36 m above sea level in the NASA SRTM 30 m terrain model.

source.title: OpenTopoData, NASA SRTM 30 m elevation at 35.65, 139.65

facts.text: The Japanese zelkova (Zelkova serrata, keyaki) is the ward tree of Setagaya.

source.title: Wikipedia (Japanese): 世田谷区
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "世田谷区", Japanese Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The brown-eared bulbul is one of the loudest and most conspicuous garden birds of lowland Japan, and was introduced to the Kantō region from further south within historical times.

source.title: Wikipedia: Brown-eared bulbul
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Brown-eared bulbul", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
